A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, geometric framework and core experiments. The main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, hidden-state geometry, attention-head ablation, denoising and task-vector experiments across seven language models.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds generation-prompt analyses, geometric intervention experiments and attention-head layer-distribution tests.

M1.justification: The stated PTH-identification rule now includes the final token position: its summation endpoint changes from s(x_i)-1 to s(x_i). v2 also extends task-vector construction to PTH outputs. The central geometric measures, logistic probing and SVD denoising remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds an open-ended food-review task using praise/critique prompts and GPT-4o-generated demonstration responses (Section 5.1; Figures 4 and 53–58). This extends evaluation beyond v1's classification tasks, while retaining the six classification datasets and Famous People scenario.

E2.justification: v1's task-vector experiment compares IH steering with zero-shot and ordinary ICL. v2 additionally compares PTH-derived and IH-derived steering directly in Figure 8 and Figures 59–64. Existing random-head ablation, demonstration-selection and zero-shot controls are retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include generation probes using the positive-minus-negative unembedding direction, PTH injection at layer 2 versus IH injection at 3L/8, and layer-distribution comparisons at four head-selection thresholds. v2 extends final-layer rank-5 denoising across models and revises the stated TREC symbol mapping. These additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's head ablations and accuracy-based IH steering, v2 tracks geometric trajectories after PTH/IH task-vector injection, directly testing their effects on separability and alignment. It also examines head layer distributions across selection thresholds and extends IH-steering analysis across models (Section 5.3; Appendix I).

E5.justification: v2 introduces Mann–Whitney U tests and p-values for PTH/IH layer distributions in Table 1 and Tables 16–21; v1 has no corresponding tests. This is a localized statistical addition, without revised seed, repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practices for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds generation and intervention trajectories, head-distribution results and further steering/denoising outcomes. New Table 24 reports Gemma-7B accuracy of 79.19% with ordinary ICL versus 66.11% with rank-5 denoising. Figure 21(a) also replaces v1 Figure 19(A)'s duplicated Gemma-2B panel with Gemma-7B results. These are additions and corrections, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, their proofs and the geometric measure definitions remain substantively unchanged. A local mathematical correction changes the PTH-score summation endpoint from s(x_i)-1 in v1 Appendix G to s(x_i) in v2 Appendix H, altering the defined score rather than merely its notation.

C1.justification: The central unification and two-stage mechanism claims are retained. v2 broadens applicability from classification to include a generation task, and its conclusion extends the alignment-based accuracy claim to generation; this is a limited extension of the original contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the warning that the framework may not extend to generation with a qualification that generation analysis is preliminary. Appendix E adds practical interpretations of existing probing and denoising techniques, while Appendix I identifies a Gemma-2B steering exception. Its claimed cross-model consistency of earlier PTH positions nevertheless exceeds the mixed findings in Table 17.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link on page 1 and documents the new generation prompts, intervention layers and PTH task-vector construction. Existing hardware, quantization, dataset caps and classifier split details are retained. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's accessibility or completeness.

R1.justification: The task-vector related-work discussion adds Merullo et al., Han et al., Kahardipraja et al. and two Jiang et al. papers. It distinguishes the present work through its account of concrete internal computation. The broader positioning around attention heads, task vectors and hidden-state geometry remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 selectively rewrites introductory, related-work and explanatory paragraphs, adds experimental subsections and a practical-implications appendix, and updates the conference header and acknowledgments. The main section organization and much of the existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: New generation and intervention plots, cross-model steering charts, significance tables and practical-result tables substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing decoded-token tables are redistributed among alignment figures, and the erroneous Gemma-7B panel is replaced. These changes extend beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The new intervention trajectories connect head outputs to hidden-state geometry more directly than v1's ablations and accuracy-only steering, while broader model checks and the corrected Gemma-7B panel improve the evidence. The net gain is limited by overinterpretation: generation accuracy is claimed without a corresponding performance evaluation, and Appendix I.3 generalizes head ordering beyond Table 17's mixed results. These issues temper the useful empirical additions.
